title: The fastest way I’ve found to debug and learn
author: Trashy_io
selftext:
I’m new-ish to coding and using AI as a learning partner, not as a autopilot.

Here’s the de-bug workflow that’s been weirdly effective for me:

1) I keep a bug.txt open while playtesting

I dump notes fast + messy, but specific. Example:

	•	Balance: make player stronger

	•	+20% base health

	•	+10% damage reduction

	•	Bug: player gets stuck

	•	check collision function

	•	check game state transitions

2) Agent #1 reads the file and turns it into:

	•	a clean task list broken into phases

	•	a quick “why it happened” report + suggested fixes

3) Agent #2 helps me implement it step-by-step

If it’s a simple fix I already understand, I’ll let it handle it. If it’s not, I do it so I actually learn.

Big rule: AI will confidently “fix” the wrong thing on bigger projects. I always review the report and make sure it matches my project structure before touching code.

Question: what’s your best debugging workflow with AI (or without)? Any tricks that beat this?

comments.author: calben99
comments.body:
Love the bug.txt workflow! That's a great way to build context over time. I use something similar but with a few tweaks:

\*\*The "Error Archaeology" Approach:\*\*
Instead of just logging bugs, I paste the actual error message + stack trace into a search. AI is shockingly good at pattern matching errors it's seen before. Even if the exact solution doesn't fit, it often points to the right direction (dependency issues, common pitfalls, etc.).

\*\*Rubber Ducking 2.0:\*\*
Before asking AI to fix something, I ask it to \*explain\* what's probably happening. "Why would this function return null here?" forces me to articulate the problem, and AI often catches gaps in my logic before I even start coding.

\*\*Context is Everything:\*\*
Your two-agent setup is smart. I've found that giving AI the "why" behind a bug helps it suggest better fixes. "This crashes when the player equips a weapon while jumping" gets better results than just "null reference exception."

\*\*One trick that's saved me:\*\* When stuck on a weird bug, I ask AI to suggest 3 possible causes before asking for fixes. It trains your intuition over time.

Great post - love seeing people use AI as a thinking partner, not just a code generator!

replies.author: Trashy_io
replies.body: Thank you so much for the response! I will definitely be implementing those into my workflow. That last one is actually a game changer!! I appreciate the kind words as well!
